chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and later years
title: Norman Granz's first Los Angeles concerts
summary: Edison recalls playing Granz's Sunday sessions for nine dollars and his first Jazz at the Philharmonic concert, with Granz fresh out of school.

blocks.x: Yeah. I mean, you know, the first time I ever saw that, he got Illinois Jacquet and you know, he was honking and screaming. But Norman knew what he was doing because the other people, you know, he had --
And Norman knew the marquee value of that because when they were screaming, that was bringing in the people.
Sure.
When I first started playing Norman Grant's concerts around here for nine dollars.
How much?
Nine dollars. This was in the '40s.
Where was that?
Right here.
Really?
Having Sunday afternoon sessions, yeah.
Oh, I see. That was like an extra.
Yeah. Well, he wasn't -- you know, he was just starting those things then. And Jo Jones, myself, Prez, Nat Cole.
Oh, you mean, you'd come out of -- you were still with Basie.

Oh, with Basie, but on a Sunday afternoon, they'd have a jazz concert at a place called the -- down on 8th and Normandy. That's where Nat got started down there. But we would have -- then he would have sessions out here on Hollywood, up here on Beverly, and on Sunday afternoons. Then I played his first concert when he named it "Jazz at the Philharmonic," here on Olive.
Well, what was Norman doing before he got into that?
Well, I think Norman was going to school mostly. I don't know what he was doing.
Oh, he was as young as that?
Yeah.
Oh, I see.
I think he'd just come out of college then.
Didn't he train for law or something?
Yeah, I think so, yeah, yeah.
